body.p: We pursued these experiments in a follow-up study that used single-cell calcium imaging with a dye applied through the recording pipette (Lei et al., 2024). We now reference this paper (p. 13).

disp-quote.p: (2) Orientation tuning and connectivity

The most developed functional results in the paper relate to the sensitivity of the WAC processes to oriented stimuli. Interpretation of these results depends on a few factors. First is the spread of signals in the WAC processes - as noted above. Second is connectivity. The paper shows that the B/K WAC activity increases inhibitory input to Off-delta and On-alpha ganglion cells. These cells, as noted in the paper, are not orientation-tuned. But the orientation-tuned ganglion cells stratify in a similar location within the IPL, and hence are situated in an appropriate place to receive input from the B/K WACs. Did you focus exclusively on connections to the Off-delta and On-alpha cells (along with the Off-alpha) or did you look at any other ganglion cell types? This should at least get discussed in more detail.

body.p: We focused on RGC types that we could routinely target based on soma size (alpha cells) or the DSGCs that we could verify based on a functional measure (p. 10). We are examining additional postsynaptic targets of B/K cells using a connectomic approach (EyeWire II dataset), which we intend to present in a future study. We note the importance of identifying additional postsynaptic targets in Discussion (p. 17).

disp-quote.p: (3) In several places it is unclear whether the paper intends to be a methods paper or a basic research paper. One example is the last sentence of the abstract. If it is intended to be a basic research paper (which is my overall impression) then I suggest shifting the emphasis in some of those key locations towards results and away from methods.

body.p: We view the project as a combination of a basic research paper and a methods paper. We prefer to keep the final sentence of the abstract.

disp-quote.p: - Fig. 1B. The GEO identifier for the dataset used to generate this plot should be cited in the legend text or methods. Also, did the authors examine expression of Opkr1 in this dataset or by immunohistochemistry? This might be useful to narrow down the transcriptomic identities of the cell types under investigation.

body.p: We downloaded data from the Broad Institute Single Cell Portal (SCP) as SCP919, by searching for the original paper at https://singlecell.broadinstitute.org/single_cell (p. 29).

disp-quote.p: - Fig. 1G. It would be helpful to also report stratification as percentage depth of the IPL to permit comparison to existing classification schemes (e.g. RGC classification of Bae et al., 2018).

body.p: We think the relative distance to the ChAT bands is the most reliable metric across studies. With that said, we provide our estimates of the nuclear boundaries in the Methods section (p. 26).

disp-quote.p: - Fig. 1F shows that some B/K cells have somas in the IPL. Do the authors have any insights as to the morphology/stratification of these cells?

body.p: We did not study these cells (p. 6).

disp-quote.p: - Fig. 2A1 and 2B1 are missing scale bars.

body.p: The 500 µm scale bar applies to all images in A and B, which we now make clear in the legend (p. 32).

disp-quote.p: - The ON cell shown in orange in Fig. 3A shows an initial fast transient response at the beginning of the ON-step that is not apparent in the OFF cells. Was this reliably observed in all the ON-type WACs? If so, it would be interesting to know more about the time course and whether there might be a contribution of voltage-gated sodium channels to this response component.

body.p: These small ‘spikelets’ were somewhat variable and difficult to quantify. We did not pursue studies of voltage-gated sodium channels at this time (p. 8, 33).

disp-quote.p: - Page 7: Fig. 3A, B The results state that "B/K WACs with dendrites in the OFF layer depolarized during the negative/OFF phase of a contrast-reversing spot stimulus, whereas B/K WACs with dendrites in the ON layer depolarized during the positive/ON phase (Fig. 3A)." It would be more accurate to characterize B/K WACs in the ON layer as hyperpolarizing during the OFF-phase since there was very little response during the ON-phase relative to background.

body.p: We reworded this as suggested (p. 8).

disp-quote.p: - Figure 5. The rise time of the control ReaChR response in the ON-alpha RGC in panel 5G seems very slow compared to the OFF-delta RGC in Fig. 5C and the OFF-alpha transient RGC example shown in Supp Fig. 1C. Was this a consistent finding, and, if so, can the authors explain the slow kinetics? There is also a marked difference in the IPSC amplitude as a function of stimulus intensity between the RGC types in Fig. 5D and 5H that warrants some explanation. Connectomic analysis of the WAC inputs to ON-sustained RGCs or paired recordings between ON-WACs and ON-sustained alpha RGCs might help establish stronger evidence for the synaptic connection between the ON-WACs and ON-sustained alpha RGCs.

body.p: We added a population analysis of time course of the optogenetic response (Fig. 5I; p. 10). We appreciate the other suggestions but cannot pursue them at this time.

disp-quote.p: - Figure 5C/G. It is unclear what the brown bars above the current traces represent (presumably the measurement time window?) - this should be added to the figure legends.

body.p: We clarified this in the legend (p. 35).

disp-quote.p: - Fig. 5B/5F - The z-voxel size should be indicated for these confocal images.

body.p: We provide the estimated z-integration given the NA of the objective lens and excitation wavelengths (~0.5 µm) (p. 26).

disp-quote.p: - Fig.6B - It would be helpful to see the WAC dendrites in this side view.

body.p: We revised the figure showing SBEM data and split it into a main figure (Fig. 6) and a supplementary figure (Figure 6-figure supplement 1). In the process, we removed the data from the original Fig. 6B, because it did not focus on WACs, and we wanted to simplify the presentation. In the future, we are pursuing more complete reconstructions of the OFF Delta connectome using EyeWire II.

disp-quote.p: - Pg 9, bottom. The text states that "Of the remaining synapses, 150 amacrine cells were reconstructed at least partially (Grimes et al., 2022), and these provided a total of 300 (out of 1020 non-AII) synapses to the OFF Delta RGC. This group comprised three classes: bistratified amacrine cells with dendrites in at the borders of the INL and GCL (Sublaminae S1 and S5) (Fig. 6B); amacrine cells with asymmetric dendritic trees (Fig. 6B); and single WAC neurites that ran unbranched through S1 of the IPL, in the same plane as the dendrites of the OFF Delta RGCs (Fig. 6C)." It would be helpful to know what proportion of the 300 non-AII synaptic inputs to the OFF Delta RGC were from WACs.

body.p: We now mention that 206/300 synapses came from WACs. With that said, the sampling was biased, as we also mention, because we focused on skeletonizing processes that appeared to come from WACs (p. 11).

disp-quote.p: - Fig. 6Dii. "Labeled somas descended beyond the volume towards the ON layer; none of the reconstructed dendrites in the OFF layer were connected to a soma within this small volume". I think this should read "Dendrites from the labeled somas descended..." ? Also, the comment about the reconstructed dendrites in the OFF layer seem like it belongs in the legend for Fig. 6Di.

body.p: We removed this section in the current version along with the figure panel, based on the limited number of labeled somas in the newly-generated SBEM dataset.

disp-quote.p: - Sign-Inverting Feedforward Inhibition (SIFI) is introduced as a term to refer to local synapses both onto presynaptic bipolar cells and onto the postsynaptic RGC, but it doesn't completely capture the key characteristics. Feed-forward inhibition is sign-inverting (SIFI). Inhibition onto bipolar dendrites is generally referred to as feedback - "SIFI" doesn't encapsulate this idea.

body.p: We see a parallel structure between feedforward inhibition and SIFI, as illustrated in Fig. 7. We prefer to keep the current description. We tried to make the similar organization of SIFI and FFI more explicit (p. 11-12).

disp-quote.p: (1) The authors used bright blue light (470 nm) to stimulate ReaChR. This light would likely activate melanopsin in ON Alpha RGCs. Did the authors observe the intrinsic photoresponse? How was this addressed in the analysis/quantification of the inhibitory currents?

body.p: We didn’t observe these. These responses run down over time (Beier et al., 2013) and would be extremely weak at the inhibitory reversal potential (Vhold = 0) used here (p. 24).

disp-quote.p: (2) Voltage clamp recordings from RGCs were shown in Fig. 5, but the Methods don't mention a conventional voltage clamp internal solution (caesium-based) or the voltage clamp protocol. Please add this.

body.p: We added a description of the Cs-based pipette solution to Methods (p. 21).

disp-quote.p: (3) Some quantification of the coverage factor for these WACs would be helpful for understanding their role in the retina. Given the dendritic structure of the cells shown in Fig. 2 and the soma density reported in Fig. 1, this should be possible to calculate.

body.p: We think that the traditional description of coverage factor is complicated for these WACs, which have very sparse dendrites and no branching. For example, drawing a convex polygon around the dendritic tree for many ON cells would leave huge gaps with no coverage (because of the lack of branches). We plan to hold off on describing the coverage of these cells until we have a better metric.

disp-quote.p: (5) Fig. 3B, it is unclear what the two lines in each color refer to. I assume one is response to positive and the other response to negative contrast, but it would be helpful to label this.

body.p: We clarified this in the legend (p. 33).

disp-quote.p: (6) In Fig 6 C and E it is very hard to tell the colors of the little dots for the synapses. Please remove the black outlines and make the dots/figures bigger.

body.p: We modified the EM data figure to improve clarity, including moving some material to supplementary figures (Figure 6, Supplementary Figure 3).

disp-quote.p: Calretinin and ChAT are used interchangeably to identify the ChAT bands and quantify stratification. The rationale for that could be described more fully in the main text. This comes up in particular in comparing Fig. 1C and 1G.

body.p: This was an historical variation. The bands in question could be labeled by either strategy (Haverkamp and Wassle, 2000) (p. 26).

disp-quote.p: Fig 2: two filled cells are shown in red, but four cells are shown in the stratification figure. Should the cells labeled a and d also be red?

body.p: The red cells in A and B correspond to the red cells in C, with lowercase letters to indicate the match between all four corresponding example cells in A/B and C. The red cells stratify between the ChAT bands. We clarified this in the legend (p. 32).

disp-quote.p: Fig. 2C and 1G could be more clearly connected (e.g. to more clearly say that one is stratification of all labeled processes and the other single cells).

body.p: For 1G, we indicate that each line comes from a z-stack of labeled processes. In 2C, we indicate that each line reflects an individual cell (p. 32).

disp-quote.p: It would be helpful for a reader to have the figure legends together with the figures to make it easier to look at them together.

body.p: We will combine these in the resubmitted version.

disp-quote.p: Fig. 3D: there is an inflection just before the hyperpolarizing component of the response of the example On cell. Was this typically the case? If so, could that suggest at least two distinct mechanistic contributions (or network effects as you allude to in the Discussion)? Related to this, in Fig. 5D the On cell inhibitory input is slower than that to the Off cell. Was this consistent, and again could that indicate network effects?

body.p: The somatic voltage responses were somewhat variable and were not quantified extensively (p. 8). We added an analysis to show the consistency of the timing differences between ON and OFF RGCs (p. 10; Fig. 5I).

disp-quote.p: Can you resolve whether the SIFI motif occurs throughout the WAC processes? For example, do you see any processes that end in the EM block, and to they show the SIFI motif near the ending?

body.p: We are pursuing this analysis in a new connectomic dataset (EyeWire II) that we plan to present in a future publication.

disp-quote.p: Figure 4E: does this use the sNMF or individual neurite segments?

body.p: It uses the individual neurite segments, as clarified now in the figure legend (p. 34).

disp-quote.p: Off delta inputs: non-ribbon inputs are assumed to be inhibitory (page 9) but there are several examples now in the literature that provide counterexamples. Those exceptions could be discussed more carefully in the text.

body.p: We commented on this point in the Methods section (p. 27).

disp-quote.p: I would add an additional sentence or two to explain the SIFI motif in more detail and relate it more clearly of feedforward and feedback inhibition.

body.p: We added a sentence of clarification (p. 11-12).

disp-quote.p: Are you able to identify an Off-delta cell in new EM block?

body.p: We were not able to identify these RGC types specifically (p. 28).

disp-quote.p: The Discussion section "WACs form a diverse group of ..." is quite broad. For example, a key conclusion of that section as currently written is at the top of page 13, "The collected findings suggest that ...". An argument could be made that there is strong support for that sentence in the literature already. I would suggest focusing that section on some of the specific findings in this paper - e.g. the results about orientation selectivity. Perhaps this section could be combined with the "Possible roles of B/K ..." section.

body.p: We decided to maintain this section, because we wanted to compare the B/K WACs to previous descriptions of WACs in the literature – many of which seem to be describing distinct cell types.

disp-quote.p: Did you fill any of the B/K WACs with neurobiotin to look for gap junctional coupling?

body.p: We have not pursued this strategy.

disp-quote.p: Limitations: I would add here that having a more complete set of ganglion cells whose responses are modulated by the B/K WACs would be a key step in evaluating their function role (e.g. do these cells shape responses of orientation-selective ganglion cells).

body.p: We added this point (p. 17).
